To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
early weaning of rats by bandage wrapping of the dam during lactation does not affect anxiety-like or memory/learning behavioral parameters at adulthood.

a model of early weaning in which lactating rat dams are wrapped in a bandage during the last three lactation days does not affect anxiety-like, novelty seeking and memory/learning behaviors of male offspring at adulthood.

the EW model in which lactating dams are wrapped with bandages to block access to pups' milk during the last days of lactation does not affect the anxiety-like, novelty seeking and memory/learning behavior of the adult male offspring, except for an increased number in the rearing events.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of a short period of breastfeeding on neurobehavioral development and the results obtained with our EW model may be relevant to the understanding of the impact of early life events on the development of psychiatric disorders.
the effects of a shortened period for breastfeeding in rodents, which is a common practice in human populations.
the effects of early weaning in the offspring, which is a relevant issue in public health since the practice of EW is widespread.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of milk withdrawal during the last three postnatal days on behavior depend on the model used.
EW in rodents may affect some aspects of behavior in adult animals, such as vertical activity, but not others, such as anxiety-like, novelty seeking or learning/memory traits.

the EW model involving wrapping of dams with a bandage, which is the least traumatic and stressful, has no effect on anxiety-like, novelty seeking and memory/learning behavior at adulthood, but does increase vertical activity in the open field arena.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bandaging method is the least stressful model of EW in rats, and it is the only model that allows the evaluation of the effects of milk withdrawal per se.

the effects of EW on the adult offspring depend on the type of model used and the time of testing, with a greater impact at the endocrine level and on anxiety-like behavior in adulthood, and on memory and learning at weaning.

EW in Wistar rats is associated with increased food intake, hyperleptinaemia, leptin resistance, hyperadrenalineemia and hyperinsulinaemia, as well as increased adrenal catecholamines, and increased anxiety-like behavior, but not novelty-seeking behavior or spatial learning and memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EW, as induced by bandaging the dam, does not seem to affect the development of anxiety-like, novelty seeking and learning/memory traits in the adult offspring.
, despite the hyperphagia and hyperleptinemic state observed in the adult offspring, EW animals do not present anxiety-like, novelty seeking or memory/learning behavioral alterations.
, although the model of EW used herein is associated with a higher body mass and hyperleptinemic and hyperinsulinemic states, it does not induce anxiety-like or novelty-seeking behavioral traits.
